products.name: CrystalWorkshop
products.summary: A modding editor for the FINAL FANTASY XIII trilogy on PC: sheets, text, models, effects, scenes, scripts and the Crystarium. It exports CrystalWorkshop Shards (.cws) that players install with PulseDepot.
features: **Sheets (WDB) and SQL**: edit typed database sheets, or query and change them with SQL. Changes show as a dry run before you apply them.
**Text (ZTR)**: every locale side by side, control tags with a tag palette, and add/rename/delete keys.
**Models**: inspect meshes, materials, textures, skeleton and motions, rendered with the game's own shaders. Round-trip through a glTF workspace (Blender) with a dry-run import.
**VFX**: package tree, typed inspector, field edits (XIII), safe model/texture reference swaps, and playback.
**Scenes (LYB)**: a 3D scene editor with fly camera, picking, move/rotate/scale gizmo, typed fields, and add/duplicate/delete of placements. XIII-2 and LR layouts are Experimental.
**Scripts, actions, events and sound**: decompile scripts to Java, edit, compile and merge (JDK 17+ needed).
**Export**: a portable .cws shard with metadata, changelog and image, or loose files for your own testing.
**AI (MCP)**: crystalw --mcp or the in-app server lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Codex use the same editors, with a read-only kill switch.

requirements: **CrystalWorkshop previews:** Bundled DXVK 3.1.1; a GPU and driver with Vulkan 1.3
**Script mods and script editing:** A JDK 17 or newer (not bundled), e.g. Eclipse Temurin
windows.label: Windows 10/11 x64

requirements: **CrystalWorkshop previews:** The system's DXVK-native (`libdxvk_d3d9.so`, e.g. Arch `libdxvk`) with SDL3 or SDL2; Vulkan 1.3
**Script mods and script editing:** A JDK 17 or newer from your distribution (not bundled)
linux.label: Linux x86_64

changelog.text: a redesigned interface with new pages and fixes. A new app layout (app bar, project explorer, status footer, command palette Ctrl+K, document tabs, icon rail), a script outline and problems drawer with token-based highlighting, a scene placement outline and viewport toolbar with an inspector showing original and current values, a multi-track cutscene timeline with transport controls and export, XIII motion clips checked with the game's own evaluation beside the preview, an effects layout with a playback timeline and typed fields, a UI Layouts page that edits and previews menu layouts for all three games, a Fonts page for the game's menu fonts, one undo history for the whole project, a redesigned Settings page with row density (Compact or Comfortable), an export wizard with a package-details step and grouped warnings, exports and AI assistants kept inside a workspace folder beside the game executable, revert one script class or a whole file (asks first and can be undone), Java script tools capped at 30% of memory, exports never drop a changed file and merge file lists, XIII scene lights no longer draw black, undo steps whose files changed since are refused, multi-byte text no longer cut in half, shards keep their name and version, unsaved work protected when you leave or switch sessions, the interface no longer freezes during background work.

knownIssues: XIII-2/LR VFX fields are read-only, and their exports are unverified in game.
Model imports apply only simple changes (no new vertices, materials or bones).
Unsigned (SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway); no installer; no AppImage.

products.name: PulseDepot

stores.name: Microsoft Store
stores.note: XIII-2 only; cannot start the game

products.summary: The mod manager for the FINAL FANTASY XIII trilogy on PC: install CrystalWorkshop shards and older Nova Chrysalia mod packages without touching your archives or your saves.
features: FF13 / XIII2 / LR tabs; each game has its own folder, list and launcher options. Steam games are detected automatically on Windows and Linux.
Add **.cws** shards and Nova Chrysalia **.ncmp**/.zip packages with Add mod… or drag and drop.
Enable, disable and order mods (later mods win). Conflicts are flagged, and text, database and WPD files are merged entry by entry.
**Review changes** shows exactly what will be installed, updated, downgraded or removed before anything is written. **Apply changes** installs the set.
Version-aware: updates replace a listed mod, downgrades ask first, and changelogs show what is new.
A clear warning for mods that ship native code.
Crux is installed and verified by SHA-256 for you: the standalone build, or the addon build when PulseDepot detects the third-party NovaFix loader.
Saves are never read or written. Mod settings live in Crux's own per-slot storage.
Game launcher (Steam), Create package, and Format tools (WPD/WDB/ZTR/filelist/TRB/SCD/xlsx/SQLite conversions).

requirements: **PulseDepot:** Windows 10/11 x64; D3D12 or Vulkan
**The game:** Steam (XIII-2 from the Microsoft Store: experimental)
**Script mods and script editing:** A JDK 17 or newer (not bundled), e.g. Eclipse Temurin
windows.label: Windows 10/11 x64

requirements: **PulseDepot:** x86_64; Vulkan or OpenGL
**The game:** Steam with Proton. The standalone Crux needs the launch option `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="version=n,b" %command%`
**Script mods and script editing:** A JDK 17 or newer from your distribution (not bundled)
linux.label: Linux x86_64

changelog.text: Redesigned interface and new pages. A new look with an icon rail (new Mods and Review pages, a details drawer for the selected mod and confirmations for danger-zone actions), a Game setup page (game folder, archive and optional data, Crux host, large memory support and Uninstall all in one place), Create package is now a wizard (Source, Details and Output steps), Format tools has a search box, a Crux settings page (choices and filters, and reset any setting to its default), an Apply result page that shows each stage of Apply (if the Crux settings could not be saved, your edits are kept so you can retry them), an Activity page (recent reviews, applies and Crux repairs for each game), Preferences for interface density and scale, a large memory support switch for the game executable (on by default; not available where Steam's DRM would reject a changed game file, so on Linux the Proton launch option PROTON_FORCE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1 is suggested instead; a change made there by an earlier PulseDepot is undone), each mod is checked against the bundled Crux before Apply (and against the raised script capacity setting when it needs it), Repair Crux installs PulseDepot's Crux into the game folder again (your mods and saves stay as they are), PulseDepot keeps its own settings in pulsedepot.json next to the program (game folders, launch options and install choices), the Crux console window is hidden by default, the Mod Settings menu (Configuration, Mod Settings) is now part of Crux and installed with it, Game setup shows the installed and bundled Crux versions and says when an update is available (an older Crux in the game folder is replaced on Apply and the review names it), mod lists saved by older versions load again and installed mods are always listed, PulseDepot reports the real state of the game executable if writing the large memory flag fails, packages are still not code-signed (Windows SmartScreen asks once) and there is no installer.
first public release. Crux in two builds with NovaFix detection, .cws shards, Nova Chrysalia package import, review/apply, changelogs and version prompts, Windows and Linux builds.

knownIssues: Tested in game on Linux (Proton); not yet tested on real Windows.
Unsigned (SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway); no installer; no AppImage on Linux.
The list cannot be reordered by drag and drop; use the ▲/▼ buttons.

changelog.title: Crux 0.2.0-beta
items: The in-game Mod Settings menu (Configuration → Mod Settings) is now built into Crux for FINAL FANTASY XIII, FINAL FANTASY XIII-2 (Steam and Microsoft Store) and LIGHTNING RETURNS: FINAL FANTASY XIII. It lists every installed mod's options in the language the game is running in. It replaces the separate Mod Settings package; PulseDepot turns the old package off.
Support for one more FINAL FANTASY XIII executable.
More room for game scripts in FINAL FANTASY XIII: up to 1024 script classes and 1024 resident battle scripts. Mods that need the extra room require this version of Crux or later.

Startup diagnostics: Crux writes a diagnostics log next to the game's add-ons that you can attach to bug reports. It records which game files and mods Crux finds, and whether the game asks Crux for mod files in the first minutes of play.
The game is still recognised after its executable has been patched to use more memory (Large Address Aware).
Help lines in Mod Settings show only the selected row's own description.
Mod Settings and the game-language detection could fail to start.

knownIssues: The Mod Settings menu on the Microsoft Store edition of FINAL FANTASY XIII-2 and on LIGHTNING RETURNS has not yet been tested in game.
